clue.text: Salad plant bird and antelope both left unfinished

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter, as 'both' covers the bird and the antelope together

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
the oryx is a large African antelope
a chick is a young bird
the oryx is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A gardener lists a salad plant, then two animals whose names trail off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both left unfinished' applies to the bird and the antelope alike: each loses its final letter before the two are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory is a leafy vegetable whose bitter leaves are eaten in salads.

clue.text: Split in church overwhelming priest in charge

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev, the Reverend, is a priest's title

explanation.surface: A rift in the church as it overpowers the priest in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelming' signals that the church abbreviation engulfs the priest's title and the in-charge abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or split in rock or a wall.

clue.text: Midwest state camp, not well disposed

parts.note: Ill. is an abbreviation for Illinois, a Midwest US state
camp means affected, theatrical and mannered

explanation.surface: A camp in a Midwest state is described as unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-affected means hostile or unfavourably inclined, the opposite of well disposed.

clue.text: African starling's neat attempt to circle rook

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox is a neat

indicators.note: to circle is to go round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: An African bird's tidy attempt to fly around a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circle' wraps the attempt round the chess rook. 'neat' is not tidy: it is an archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-bird is an African oxpecker, a kind of starling that perches on cattle.

clue.text: Weak-kneed footballer's cheap novel

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, lacking nerve
a back is a defensive footballer

explanation.surface: A timid footballer turns out to have written a cheap paperback.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowback was a cheap Victorian novel sold in yellow board covers.

clue.text: Commonplace to smell drink daughter's imbibed

parts.note: in British slang to hum is to give off a bad smell
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone says it's ordinary to smell drink on a daughter who has been at the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibed' puts the daughter inside the drink. 'smell' uses British slang, where to hum is to stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull and ordinary, a close synonym of commonplace.

clue.text: With effort, draw college building, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that a word is to be taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a hall is a college building, e.g. a hall of residence

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a sketch of a university hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' gives the sound of HALL, spelt HAUL in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul is to pull or drag something heavy with effort.

clue.text: Shaker's companion touring Pacific state also

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: movers and shakers go together, so a mover accompanies a shaker
Ore. is an abbreviation for Oregon, on the Pacific coast

explanation.surface: A Shaker and friend tour a Pacific state as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the companion round the Pacific state. 'Shaker' suggests the religious sect, but it comes from the phrase 'movers and shakers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover means besides, in addition, which is the sense of also.

clue.text: Practical joke played by Scott Joplin?

definitions.meaning: a prank, especially a student stunt

explanation.definitionFit: Rag means both a prank and a ragtime composition like Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag.

clue.text: The name contrived for the simplest hydrocarbon

indicators.note: contrived means artificially made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist invents a name for the most basic compound of carbon and hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges THE and NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane, CH4, is the simplest hydrocarbon, with a single carbon atom.

clue.text: Scoundrel in Albert Square, a slippery type

indicators.note: Albert Square is the setting of the soap EastEnders, where Cockney speakers drop their initial H

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy man

explanation.surface: A villain in a London soap's square is described as a slippery customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Square is the fictional East London square in the BBC soap EastEnders; Cockneys drop the H, so HEEL becomes 'EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are proverbially slippery, so the fish fits the description of something hard to grasp.

clue.text: Standing stiffly, conductor listened to piano

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard rather than read, so the conductor's name gives its sound

parts.note: Sir Adrian Boult was a celebrated English orchestral conductor
an upright is a piano with vertical strings

explanation.surface: A concert-goer notes the conductor standing stiffly, listening to the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listened to' turns BOULT, the English conductor Sir Adrian Boult, into its sound BOLT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolt upright is an idiom for sitting or standing perfectly straight and rigid.

clue.text: Make deduction to cover port that's substandard

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to infer is to make a deduction
Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: An inspector reasons that a port's goods are not up to standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior is a synonym of substandard, meaning lower in quality.

clue.text: Having left old state, soldier enters arcade

indicators.note: the soldier enters the state, so one abbreviation goes inside the other

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier, having left his old state, wanders into a shopping arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts the soldier inside the state's postal abbreviation; 'Having' is a link, and 'old' is its own abbreviation, not part of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an open-sided gallery or arcade along a building.

clue.text: Sombre Australian's role in Hamlet

parts.note: grave means serious and sombre
digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A serious Australian actor lands a part in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: The gravedigger is the clown who digs Ophelia's grave in Act 5 of Hamlet.

clue.text: Sweeping extra study, accepting scant payment at first

parts.note: a wide is an extra in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to read is to study, as in reading law

explanation.surface: A sweeping additional study that takes on little pay at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of scant payment; 'accepting' puts them inside the word for study. In cricket, a wide is a run awarded as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread and sweeping both describe something extensive and far-reaching.

clue.text: Flat race possibly isn't long enough

indicators.note: the word falls short, so its last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a race is one example of a sporting event

explanation.surface: A flat race may not be run over a long enough distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't long enough' cuts the final T from EVENT. 'Flat race' reads as one horse-racing term but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level or flat, as in an even surface.

clue.text: Destroy monastic type adopting new rite

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an oblate is a lay person dedicated to a monastery

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the word rite made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A monk is urged to destroy tradition by taking up a new rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of rite, and 'adopting' puts the result inside the word for a monastic lay member.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, a strong synonym of destroy.

clue.text: Hesitation in a right toff's reasoning …

indicators.note: in places the hesitation inside the following pieces

parts.note: a toff is a gentleman, a gent
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A posh gent hesitates as he makes his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts UM inside ARGENT, after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a line of reasoning set out to support a case.

clue.text: Ballet teachers take the biscuit!

parts.note: NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teachers' union
a cracker is a thin dry biscuit

explanation.surface: An exclamation that teachers' behaviour at the ballet is beyond belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the biscuit' is British for being outrageous, but here 'take' simply joins NUT, the old National Union of Teachers, to CRACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nutcracker is Tchaikovsky's famous Christmas ballet.

clue.text: … can put up charge for fertiliser

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a tin is a can
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Continuing the thought, a can be raised and a fee charged for fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TIN round; the ellipsis links to the previous clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen compounds widely used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Cut down animal skin

definitions.meaning: to ... a tree is to cut it down
a hide or pelt with its hair

explanation.definitionFit: Fell is both a verb for chopping down trees and an old noun for a pelt.

clue.text: Late riser told untruths about president

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: lied means told untruths
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

explanation.surface: A sleepyhead lied about the president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the untruths round Lincoln's short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who stays in bed late in the morning.

clue.text: Place of torment — for instance, Greece?

parts.note: hell is the place of eternal torment
as means for instance, as in 'cities such as Rome'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Greece is a hellish place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellas is the Greek name for Greece.

clue.text: Dullness of English girl housed by corporation

indicators.note: housed by means kept inside, so the pieces go within the other word

parts.note: corporation is jocular British slang for a paunch, a tum
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A dull English girl is employed by a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housed by' puts English and the girl inside the belly; 'corporation' is old jokey British slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of being tedious, i.e. dullness or boredom.

clue.text: Desire to get tipsy, say, after a university course

indicators.note: after places the drink-related piece behind the earlier ones

parts.note: PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree course

indicators.note: say signals a sound-alike: the word for drunk spoken, then spelt differently

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk or tipsy

explanation.surface: A student wants to get drunk after finishing a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of the word for drunk, spelt differently; 'after' puts it behind the article and the Oxford degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a craving or desire for something.

clue.text: Run round front of ruined farm building

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a bye is a run in cricket scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone runs around a ruined barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives R from ruined; 'round' puts BYE around it. A bye is a cricket run scored without the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, a farm building for cattle.

clue.text: Like those in perfect health? That's as may be

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase describes people who are entirely in good health
a grudging concession, accepting a point while doubting it matters

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom concedes a point reluctantly, while its literal words describe people feeling fine.

clue.text: Garland sure to be abandoned in free time

indicators.note: to be abandoned in means taken out of, so the word is removed from the longer one

parts.note: leisure is free time

explanation.surface: Someone is certain a garland will be left lying about on a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be abandoned in' removes SURE from LEISURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers.

clue.text: Speaker's gift shopper rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a shopper is a shopping bag

explanation.surface: A shopper turns down a present from a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns BAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: The gift of the gab is a talent for fluent speech.

clue.text: Disturbed sleep? It's something Romans accepted

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of the fodder are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: the 's is not a letter, leaving it as written

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans are said to have put up with a broken night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges SLEEP and IT. Paul's letter to the Romans is an epistle they received.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's Epistle to the Romans is a New Testament letter received by Rome's Christians.

clue.text: Wanted: teacher for involvement in exploit

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one piece within the other

parts.note: an exploit is a bold deed
Sir is how pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A wanted notice seeks a teacher for a part in some daring venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement in' puts the schoolboy's address to a teacher inside the exploit; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired and wanted are synonyms, both meaning longed for.
